cost: TWO OF EIGHT SUBJECTS ARE NOT REACHED AND ONE OF THEM IS NOT THIS FILE'S NUMBER. Dominique Wilkins '86 asked 85 +-4 and reads 76; 81 is unreachable in compute_ovr. His zone pair is rim 60 / mid 56 for a 30.3-ppg scorer, so his second-zone clearance is 33 and there is nothing to transfer. He is dominated by Patrick Ewing '90 — pinned 85 +-1 with one point of room — on efficiency (44 v 87), rim (60 v 97) and mid (56 v 67), and leads him only on ballsec (95 v 62), volume (98 v 91) and orb (74 v 63); no monotone reweighting of the bars this file pays opens a twelve-point gap between two cards in that order, and ballsec's own era slope runs the WRONG way (the 1980s primary-option class averages 83.7 against 70.3 today). Round 193's ceiling proof already has his answer: forcing rim = mid = 99 on the pre-1997 inference puts him at exactly 85. WILKINS IS A STATS-TO-RATINGS CARD.

SCOTTIE PIPPEN '92 asked 80 +-3, reads 75, frontier 76. Clearance 38 at a 1992 era share of 0.525 and a scoring load of 72 (load factor 0.68): he needs the weight at about 0.23, and Ewing '90 leaves his band at 0.16. Raising his load factor by widening recal_131's line to 45 -> 70 reaches 77 for him but costs Hakeem '90 as well as '93 and puts Kevin Johnson '92 on his own edge; it was measured and not taken.

TWO PINS SPENT, BOTH OFFERED BY TOMER IN THE DISPATCH, AND ONLY ONE WAS NEEDED. Hakeem Olajuwon '93 (recal_50, 88 +-1) is a PROVEN blocker and not a casualty: he and Kareem '80 carry the same clearance (58), the same creation factor and the same load, so this term pays them in the fixed ratio 0.942*0.84 / 0.392 = 2.019 whatever its weight or saturation is — while Kareem needs 4.542 of std to clear his band and recal_50 may take at most 2.218, a ratio of 2.048. No parameterisation of the term reaches Kareem with that pin standing. Hakeem '94 (recal_51, 88 +-1) is superseded by Tomer's own ruling on the same card. HAKEEM '90 (recal_52, 73 +-1) WAS OFFERED AND IS NOT SPENT: he reads 74 and holds.

THE BAND ANCHORS ARE NOT RE-DERIVED. OFF_TOP stays at recal_90's 102.75 and DEF_TOP at recal_102's 104.25; the round's raw maximum is unchanged in the sense that matters (Michael Jordan '89 was already the pre-1997 summit and he was already above the knee), so no card above the knee is stretched differently than it was. data/build_ratings.py WAS RUN (the chain is the full one) but nothing in it changed except PIPELINE_VERSION, so public/provenance.json and every attribute are byte-identical to v188. The round is a compute_ovr round.

ROUND 191's LEAD-HANDLER'S FLOOR IS DISJOINT BY CONSTRUCTION: it adds a floor for guards, this round adds a term to the zone block keyed on the inferred-zone flag. The two do not touch the same expression and the integrator can fold both; if they land together the combined weight should be re-swept against Ewing '90, who is this round's wall with 0.21 of raw to spare.
notes: THE MEASUREMENT THAT CAME FIRST, ON THE WHOLE POOL, BEFORE ANYTHING WAS CHANGED. Take each season's PRIMARY-OPTION CLASS: the cards with volume >= 85. That class is era-CONSTANT by construction, because `volume` is a SEASON percentile in build_ratings (Pvol is built from that season's rows) — it holds 19 to 30 cards in every one of the 47 seasons and its mean volume is 91.0 +-0.5 in all of them. Its mean OFF is 74.7 across 1980-92 and 83.8 across 2017-26. Nine points, for the same job.

THE o_score's OWN TERMS SAY WHERE THE NINE POINTS ARE (class means, 1980-92 -> 2017-26, in std units): volume 23.7 -> 23.8 FLAT, efficiency 6.2 -> 6.4 FLAT, signature 4.1 -> 4.2 FLAT — the three season-graded bars, and their flatness across 47 years is what era-graded looks like. ballsec 8.2 -> 6.8 and orb 2.8 -> 2.2 run the OTHER way (the 1980s are paid more). What is left is fouldraw +2.1, playvol 8.4 -> 13.1 (+4.7) and the ZONE BLOCK 23.0 -> 27.4 (+4.4). Inside the zone block the second-and-third slots carry half of the drift — 0.08*z1 + 0.05*z2 runs 6.0 -> 8.3 while 0.22*z0 runs 17.2 -> 19.4 — and the class's THIRD ZONE is the whole story of that half: its mean 3pt bar reads 18.1 in 1980 and 68.6 in 2026.

THE DEFECT, IN ONE SENTENCE. The zone vector 0.22 / 0.08 / 0.05 describes a THREE-ZONE GAME. A 1980s primary option played a two-zone game — the pool's own season mean of the 3pt bar is 15.1 in 1981 against 58.3 in 2025 — so his second zone was not his third option, it was his diet's other half, and the vector pays it 0.08, the weight of a third option in a game that has three. He is graded on a shot chart his league did not have.

WHY THE TRANSFER IS PAID ON (z1 - z2) AND NOT ON z1. The question the term asks is whether the card's diet actually had a third zone. Magic Johnson '90 (rim 70 / mid 60 / 3pt 60) says yes — he shot the three at the 1990 level of a modern wing — so his clearance is zero and he is byte-identical, which is how a round that lifts his entire era leaves his 93 +-1 alone. Larry Bird '84 (3pt 42) half says yes: clearance 31, the smallest transfer of the six subjects. George Gervin '80 (3pt 26 under a mid of 96) says no.

THE REJECTED SHAPES, ALL MEASURED ON THE FULL POOL AGAINST EVERY ANCHOR. (a) A UNIFORM ERA LIFT — re-centre playvol and the zone block on each season's own class level: it reaches six subjects but breaks Ewing '90, Magic '90, Shaq '94, Shaq '95, Moses '82 and Kevin Johnson '92, because a uniform shift cannot close a WITHIN-era gap and every one of those pins is a pre-1997 card. (b) THE ROLE-SPLIT READING — pay the scoring load more where the league split scoring from creation, k*max(0, volume - playvol): Ewing '90's gap is 58 and Wilkins '86's is 62, a ratio of 1.07 where 7.5 is needed; dead on arrival. (c) A USAGE-ADJUSTED EFFICIENCY with saturation at 99: reaches Wilkins by +1.43 of std where +7.68 is needed. (d) RAISING THE z[1] WEIGHT GLOBALLY: it lands six subjects at delta 0.029 and breaks nearly every modern +-1 pin, since the modern primary-option class averages z1 = 76. (e) recal_49's self-creation factor VERBATIM, with its 0.35 floor: infeasible by 5% — Ewing '90 then takes 0.66 of the transfer against Kareem '80's 0.98.

MEASURED BEFORE APPLYING, ON THE WHOLE POOL. 705 of 10,000 cards move on OFF, every one of them UP and every one of them pre-1997; histogram +1:278, +2:164, +3:119, +4:60, +5:61, +6:21, +7:2. OVR follows on 591. DEF moves on ZERO. ZERO cards from 1997 on move at all. The top 12 by OFF is identical name for name. The pre-1997 top 20 keeps Michael Jordan and Magic Johnson at its head; the entrants are Adrian Dantley '81/'82/'84, Julius Erving '80 and Michael Jordan '85.

THE CLASS IS FOUND BY THE TERM, NOT BY A NAME, AND IT READS LIKE THE RULING. The largest movers are Alex English '81-'85 (+6 to +7), Kareem Abdul-Jabbar '81 (+7), Bernard King '83, Mark Aguirre '84, Walter Davis '80-'83, George Gervin '81/'83, Andrew Toney '82/'83, David Thompson '81/'82, Julius Erving '83, Gus Williams '80, Rolando Blackman '86, Purvis Short '80/'81 — the two-zone volume scorers of 1980-86, which is the class Tomer named. The primary-option class's mean OFF goes 75.7 -> 78.7 in 1980, 73.1 -> 75.2 in 1986, 76.1 -> 78.1 in 1990, 75.1 -> 75.9 in 1994 and 79.1 -> 79.3 in 1996, against a modern class that does not move at all: the era ramp closes about a third of the nine-point gap and leaves the rest where the measurement could not justify moving it.
